turnaround_reason: A beauty/fragrance turnaround that stalled: Consumer Beauty underperformance, margin pressure, a withdrawn 2026 guidance, and the exit of CEO Sue Nabi took the stock to ~$2.79 (from a $4.56 high). Thesis rests on a new 'Coty.Curated' prestige-focused strategy and debt paydown from divesting the Gucci license.
bullish_points: Returning the Gucci Beauty license to Kering for ~$400M to cut debt and refocus on core prestige fragrance
Prestige fragrance still the resilient piece; Marc Jacobs Beauty relaunch positioned as a defining 2026 launch
Optically cheap on assets: P/B ~0.82, fwd P/E ~10.9; high insider ownership (~59%)
Positive FCF (~$363M TTM) despite the operational mess
bearish_points: Guidance withdrawn and CEO gone — leadership vacuum with only an interim CEO running a 'comprehensive review'; lawsuits add noise
Consumer Beauty down ~10% like-for-like; the mass color-cosmetics business is under strategic review (i.e. possibly shrinking/selling from weakness)
Negative operating and profit margins (-2.4% / -10.4%); recent quarters missed badly (EPS -0.02 vs -0.01)
Analyst target mean $2.69 is BELOW the current price — the Street sees no upside, and net debt is still ~$3.3B (D/E 98)
catalyst: A new permanent CEO with a credible plan and visible debt reduction from the Gucci divestiture proceeds
catalyst_timing: Q1 FY27 earnings 2026-11-05; permanent-CEO appointment TBD
suggested_trade: Pass / watch-only for now. If taken, keep it a token spot under $2.60 and wait for a permanent CEO plus a de-levering milestone before committing.
key_risk: The interim leadership + strategic-review limbo drags on while Consumer Beauty keeps eroding, so the divestiture cash just plugs holes instead of funding a real turnaround.
would_skip_if: No permanent CEO / no clear plan by the next print, or Consumer Beauty declines steepen despite the divestiture.
